headline_tiles: vocabulary collapse at equal proteins sampled

blocks.html: Seadornaviruses are mosquito-borne. Banna virus is the one that matters clinically — it has been isolated from patients with encephalitis in China, Vietnam and Indonesia — and the other three species are known mainly from mosquito pools.

rows: genomes in the BV-BRC protein dump

blocks.html: Parts-per-name peaks at exactly 12 across 44 strain names, which is both the ICTV segment count and the evidence that the grouping key used to reassemble these genomes is right. Every record in this family's BV-BRC dump is a single segment; the routing and coverage figures below are measured on 46 genomes reassembled from records sharing a strain name and contributing exactly twelve segments.

This is a small module. 1,202 protein features, 793 unique sequences, 696 of them in a collection — against 48,007 for Rotavirus. Banna virus supplies roughly half. Every number below should be read with that in mind.

sections.lede: One genus, one module, and nothing about the genome organisation is in doubt.
sections.title: What the module covers

blocks.html: The rule list binds the explicit VP1–VP12 forms plus one descriptive string. Every other synonym was tested against the length distribution of the sequences carrying it, the procedure this project adopted after the Orbivirus build, and all but one covered more than one protein: nonstructural protein sits on 41 records matching no feature at all and 29 matching VP11; outer capsid protein on VP12 24 times and VP10 3.
The one that binds is dsRNA binding protein — 38 occurrences, every one of them VP12. That is the protein's actual function, and nothing else in the genus is annotated that way.

RNA-dependent RNA polymerase failed the test again. On 12 records it sits on VP1 six times, VP2 once, and three times on something matching no feature. Orbivirus gave the same result. Twice is a pattern, so this project now never binds that string by rule in any taxon, even though it names the polymerase wherever one exists: a few deposits always put it on the wrong protein, and the homology rescue can separate them per sequence where a rule cannot.
89.2% of features bound by rule and the rescue took the rest. Nothing was left unassigned.

sections.lede: Twelve collections, one per segment, and the descriptive synonyms tested before any of them was trusted.
sections.title: How it was built

blocks.html: The generated cutoff for VP11 admitted 161 sequences that are not VP11. The formula scales with protein length and VP11 is 180 residues, so it produced 30 bits — low enough to admit sequence that is not the protein at all. Scoring every PSSM against every collection and taking the best hit per sequence gave the correction: VP10 30→75, VP11 30→165, VP12 30→140, each admitting zero false positives while keeping 98–100% of true members. This was done before the panel ran rather than after it, which is the one procedural thing this module did better than Orbivirus.

The nine long features stay at 60 even though VP5 shows 56 cross-hits above it and VP6 45. Those two are each other: outside Banna virus both run about 505 residues and are genuinely similar. Separating two real proteins is the annotator's best-hit rule's job, not the cutoff's. The zero-cross-hit criterion wanted VP5 raised to 310, which is the same over-correction that proposed 990 for Orbivirus VP3.

Self-recall against each feature's own in-range collection: 694 of 696 (99.7%) — VP1 53/53, VP2 52/52, VP3 55/55, VP4 46/46, VP5 45/45, VP6 56/56, VP7 48/48, VP8 48/48, VP9 63/63, VP10 86/86, VP11 48/49, VP12 94/95. This is a floor, not a validation; the held-out figures are in §05 and §06.

rows: genomes ≥ 5 kb, clustered at 95% nucleotide identity

blocks.html: 6 rep contigs ship with the module, each one a whole 12-segment genome; 6 of them are the best BLASTn hit for at least one exemplar. Every incoming record in this family is a single segment, so a segment routes if it resembles any segment of any chosen reference; that is the model the reference set was chosen under.

The question was whether 46 complete genomes could support a reference set at all — a taxon that cannot reach most of itself inside the budget is tabled rather than forced, which is what happened to Endornaviridae at 30%. Clustering segments and choosing genomes greedily by uncovered segment clusters, five references reach 100%. Six ship.
That is the segment-level model: every incoming record is one segment, a rep contig is a whole genome carrying all twelve, so a segment routes if it resembles any segment of any chosen reference.

sections.lede: Routing was the go/no-go for this module, and it passed immediately.
sections.title: Does it route?

blocks.html: 19 of 19 routed exemplars get every one of the 12 core features. No core feature trails the best-called one by 20 points or more.

Twelve of twelve at 100%. There is no lineage-specific accessory here, no overlapping ORF and no protein that part of the genus lacks, so there is nothing to exclude from the core count and not_universal is empty — the only module in this family where that is true.

sections.lede: Every feature is called in every routed exemplar.
sections.title: Does it call the proteins?

blocks.html: The panel is 40 genomes drawn round-robin across species from this genus's own BV-BRC contigs, with every rep-contig reference genome excluded, built into GTOs with rast-create-genome and scored by viral_genome_quality.pl. Genuinely clean means no genome, contig or feature flag at all.

blocks.html: Every non-reference genome in the dump is in the panel, so this is the whole module tested against itself minus its six references. 33 of 40 are genuinely clean and none called nothing.

Every flag is a property of the deposit, not of the module. 22 are Contig has too many ambiguous bases, 8 Contig is too short, one each too long and missing. There is not a single missing-essential flag in the run — the only module in this family of which that is true.
By species: all 7 Kadipiro genomes clean, 23 of 26 Banna, 3 of 5 Liao ning. The single Mangshi and single unclassified genome are both flagged, both for ambiguous bases.

sections.lede: Forty genomes held out of the build, annotated end to end and scored by the genome quality tool.
sections.title: Are the calls right?

blocks.html: It is built on 696 sequences. That is the whole limitation and everything else follows from it. Eleven features at 100% on a held-out panel is the easiest result in this family, and it should be read as this module describes its own dump well rather than as a claim about seadornaviruses in general.

Mangshi virus contributes 36 records to the entire genus. Its profiles rest on very few independent observations, and self-recall cannot distinguish a profile that generalises from one that has memorised four training sequences. The same caution applies in weaker form to Liao ning and Kadipiro.

VP5 and VP6 are not cleanly separable outside Banna virus. Both run about 505 residues in the other three species and cross-match each other's profiles. The annotator's best-hit rule resolves it in practice — both are called in 100% of the panel — but the margin is thinner than the numbers suggest, and a genuinely novel seadornavirus could land on the wrong one.
Reassortment is not modelled. Segments are annotated independently.

Complete for the genus as deposited, with twelve features called in essentially every genome. The honest caveat is size rather than any specific gap: this is a 696-sequence module, and its perfect scores are easier to earn than Rotavirus's.

The contamination audit reported 99 moves — 14% of the module — and every one of them was wrong. The tool compared each sequence to one canonical per feature, taken from that feature's largest cluster. Banna virus is half the dump, so it won every largest-cluster, and all twelve canonicals were Banna. The Kadipiro, Liao ning and Mangshi proteins then matched whichever Banna canonical was nearest.

The symmetry is what gave it away: VP5→VP6 24 and VP6→VP5 24, equal in both directions. Real contamination runs one way, because it comes from mislabelled deposits. Applying those moves would have shuffled three species' proteins at random. The tool now takes one reference per cluster rather than per feature, so a divergent species is judged against its own lineage wherever one exists; the count drops to 8, and all 8 verify by length and margin.

Only 0.0% of this dump declares itself partial, matching Orbivirus and against 39% for Rotavirus. The difference is deposit practice: rotavirus VP4 and VP7 are genotyping targets routinely sequenced in part, while seadornavirus deposits are whole segments.

sections.lede: What the run turned up that was not expected.
sections.title: What the run found

blocks.html: Rarefaction over proteins: every annotated protein in the 40 genomes both sources annotate (487 source product records, 482 module calls) shuffled 100 times and drawn one at a time. Both curves start at zero. The source vocabulary reaches 60 distinct strings, the module's 12. At the depth both reach, 482 proteins, free text has used 59.8 strings against 12.0 — a 5.0-fold difference. The source reaches 95% of its final size after 420 proteins, the module after 33.

93 distinct source strings collapse onto 12 annotations. The unbound tail is 8 strings, led by nonstructural protein — a label that names a class rather than a protein and that the rescue could not resolve to one.

The rarefaction is the more honest form of the claim because it controls for sampling depth: drawing annotated proteins one at a time, free text reaches 60 distinct strings and the module's vocabulary reaches 12. The collapse is smaller than Rotavirus's 12.1-fold or Orbivirus's 10.8-fold for the same reason everything here is smaller — fewer depositors have had the chance to invent a new spelling.

standfirst: Banna, Kadipiro, Liao ning and Mangshi virus: twelve double-stranded RNA segments, twelve proteins, one per segment. The smallest module in Sedoreoviridae and the only one with no derived features, no overlapping ORFs and no homology split. This audit says what it covers and what its size means.
title: Seadornavirus Coverage Audit
